topics.topic: Ownership of A06 ordering rules, including unwritten import mappings
questions: Who owns and performs A06 ordering for an import mapping that has not been written to the SQLite store?
Are list ordering rules owned by `store`, or by each domain module with `store` merely executing an order specification supplied to it?

quotes: A06: the order of every list read — each key as A06 names it, text by Unicode code point, every key ending in an identity or a sequence number — so no module sorts records itself.

M01, M02 and M03 and their records: A01 — every create carries a request id, a repeat answers the record unchanged when its facts equal the record's current ones, a different one is refused, lookup among the same project's records for a room, a repeat checked only through stage (4) — and, for 'add a room', its project's archive check; a project's repeat answers an archived project as it stands (A01 rule 3, test 4) — the request id leaving with the values erasure removes (rules
2–9; the pointer's publish under the same rules is `artifact_pointers'`, the
Customer's create `customers'`); A03 for projects; the revision and
last-changed instant (A04 rules 1–3 for projects); the project's lifecycle —
archive, anonymise, delete whole (M01) — and its repeated transitions (A05);
rooms, added and never changed (M03); the project card, `context`,
`validate` and the project's part of the agent projection; lists in A06
rules 1, 2 and 8's orders. A05 rule 4's refusals that are project ones.
judgement.divergence: The store-owned interpretation requires every list and import mapping to receive A06 ordering from `store`; the domain-owned interpretation lets `migration_import` and the other record modules determine their own A06 ordering. The owner sees different mapping orders for equivalent files.
judgement.why: The text assigns ownership of A06 ordering both to `store` and to record modules, while forbidding modules from sorting records themselves.

topics.topic: Ownership of A17 startup-check failure precedence across configuration, backup probing, and store opening
questions: Which module owns the complete A17 failure-precedence order across configuration-only checks, the backup probe and store opening?
Which module owns the complete first-failure order across configuration validation, backup probing and store opening?

quotes:
The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, serving nothing until every check passed (A17 rule 2); the
owner-only start (A17 rule 1, A18 rule 9); the two surfaces; the 60-second pass
of `owner_sessions` and the minute look of `backups` (A13 rule 2, A18 rule 1);
that a restart ends every owner session (A13 rule 2).
judgement.why: `instance_lifecycle` owns the cross-module precedence: configuration validation, then the backup probe, then store opening; each called module owns only its own checks.

topics.topic: Dependency-safe generation of confirmation IDs only for accepted audit erasures
questions: How does `audit_log`, which decides whether the erasure is accepted and writes its entry, obtain the confirmation id from `operations` without minting one for a refused action or depending back on `operations`/`random_values`?

quotes:
No other module appends an entry; the erasure of old
  entries is the one action whose entry `audit_log` writes itself, inside
  `erase_audit_entries_before` (A15 rule 4), and `operations` appends none
  for it.

A14 rules 1 and 5:
appending the audit entry in the action's transaction when the action changed
state, and minting the confirmation id only then — but for the erasure of old
audit entries, which mints one whenever it is accepted, also when it removes
nothing (A14 rule 5, A15 rule 6).

Whether an action changed state (the action's module says), minting the
confirmation id (`operations`), who may read the log (`operations` and

judgement.divergence: One implementation has `operations` pre-mint a confirmation id before `audit_log` validates the date, consuming a random UUID on a refusal; another mints only after validation or introduces a callback/capability, so the refusal consumes none. The owner reading the later accepted audit entry, and deterministic tests, observe a different confirmation id.
judgement.why: The audit module owns acceptance and entry creation but cannot know `operations` or `random_values`, while `operations` must mint the id only after acceptance and no dependency-safe handshake is defined.

topics.topic: Ownership and capability for atomically capturing backup snapshot metadata
questions: Which module captures the backup instant and audit sequence inside the same read transaction as the copied store, and through what dependency-safe capability?

quotes:
For a backup (A18 rules 1, 2): one consistent read snapshot of the whole store,
written as a store file of its own at the temporary path `backups` names and
makes for it, with the agent
sessions removed from that copy, so it passes the same checks; and the full
integrity and version check of such a file, the decrypted copy included,
opened for reading only.

A18: the daily run at 03:00 UTC while Registry runs with its tokens, from the
minute look and the dates the process remembers (rule 1); the copy, without
agent sessions, that `store` writes at the temporary path `backups` names
(rule 2), encrypted with the configured key, recording its
instant, release, last sequence number and key digest (rules 1, 3); the three
steps — removing temporary files, writing and checking the backup by
decrypting it and asking `store` to check the copy, deleting backups older
than 30 × 24 hours and unreadable ones (rule 4); the prefixes and the location
rules (rule 5), the probe file of A17 rule 2; the newest kept backup's instant
for the owner interface. No run in an owner-only start (rule 9).

The last sequence number its
store ever wrote, for a backup's record (A18 rule 1).

Every recorded instant is read from `clock.recorded_now`; every
limit of A13 and the minute look of A18 rule 1 from `clock.monotonic_reading`
and `clock.recorded_now`. No other module reads a clock.
judgement.divergence: One implementation makes `store` capture the snapshot-begin instant and in-snapshot sequence and return them with the copy; another lets `backups` read the clock and query `audit_log` separately, allowing sequence 11 or a later instant to describe a copy containing only sequence 10. Backup checking and the owner monitoring it observe the difference.
judgement.why: The snapshot, its timestamp, and its sequence metadata have separate owners, but no module or capability owns their atomic capture inside the same read transaction.

witness.initial: The store's last audit sequence is 10 and a backup run begins while another accepted change is about to commit sequence 11.
events: The daily backup run asks `store` for a consistent snapshot.
The concurrent accepted change commits sequence 11.
The backup record obtains its instant and last sequence metadata.
outcomes: The metadata is captured with the snapshot, so it records sequence 10 and the instant at which the snapshot transaction began.
The metadata is read separately, so it records sequence 11 or an instant outside the snapshot transaction while the copied store still contains sequence 10.
witness.observer: The owner monitoring the backup run or later inspecting the backup record.
basis:
A backup is a consistent copy of the store taken while Registry runs:
   one snapshot of the store, as one read transaction sees it, while other
   transactions go on; it never holds part of a transaction, and its
   recorded instant and last sequence number are those of that snapshot,
   the instant being when its read transaction began.

topics.topic: Ownership of kept and temporary backup filename prefixes
questions: Does `release_declarations` own the prefix values with `backups` only enforcing and using them, or may `backups` define the prefix values itself?

quotes:
What a release declares and a running instance reads from it alone: A22 — the
artifact types with their owner services, the first release's one type
(`estimate`, PresuPro) — A09 rule 2's table of the services, their operations
and their highest classes; the store version; the store's temporary-name
suffix (A17 rule 5); the kept and temporary backup prefixes, neither beginning
with the other (A18 rule 5); the import file's size limit (A19 rule 4, its
value State 6's); the release's own version and its contract version: every

judgement.divergence: One implementation has `operations` or `migration_import` read one import instant and pass it to every participating module; another lets each module read `clock.recorded_now` when writing its record. The owner reading imported Customers, the closure, and the audit log observes equal versus differing instants.
judgement.why: The texts require an import instant but assign neither ownership of that action-wide fact nor a capability that distributes one clock reading to all modules in the transaction.

witness.initial: A valid import will create two Customers, and the recorded clock advances between record writes.
events: The two imported Customers are written.
The migration closure and import audit entry are written in the same transaction.
outcomes: Both Customers, the closure and the audit entry receive one import instant captured for the action.
Each owning module reads `clock.recorded_now` independently, so the Customers, closure and audit entry may carry different instants.
witness.observer: The owner reading the Customers and audit log, or code comparing imported records with the migration closure.
